title: The Periodic Table
seo_title: Year 10 Science: The Periodic Table Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Explain how the structure and properties of atoms relate to the organisation of the elements in the periodic table (Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 10 science worksheets on the periodic table: groups and periods, electron shells and valence electrons, metals, non-metals and metalloids, alkali metals, halogens, noble gases and reactivity trends. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons, so they react in similar ways.
body_html:
How to think about it

The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number.

  • Groups (columns): same number of valence electrons and similar properties. Periods (rows): same number of shells.
  • Metals are on the left and middle, non-metals on the right, metalloids along the staircase between them.
  • Group 1 gets more reactive down the group; group 17 gets less reactive; group 18 (noble gases) hardly react.
Example

Chlorine: 17 electrons. Arrangement and group?

2, 8, 7

7 valence electrons

Answer: group 17, period 3

Example

Which is more reactive: sodium or potassium?

potassium is lower in group 1

Answer: potassium

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the period number is the number of valence electrons.
  • Thinking reactivity increases up group 1.
  • Thinking noble gases react easily.

faq.q: Why do elements in the same group react in similar ways?
faq.a: They have the same number of electrons in their outer shell, and these valence electrons decide how an atom reacts.

faq.q: Why is the periodic table arranged by atomic number, not mass?
faq.a: Arranging by atomic number (number of protons) puts every element in a group with similar properties. Mass order had some elements in the wrong place.
In 1869 he arranged the known elements by their properties and left gaps for undiscovered elements, predicting their properties correctly.

items.q: Roughly how big is an atom?
items.e: The nucleus is about 1/10 000 of that.

items.q: Why do noble gases rarely react?
items.e: Stable electron arrangement.

items.q: Why did Mendeleev leave gaps in his periodic table in 1869?

items.e: Gallium and germanium were later found to fit.

items.q: What did James Chadwick contribute?

He arranged the elements by atomic mass and left gaps for undiscovered elements.
He suggested electrons orbit the nucleus at fixed distances (shells).
items.e: Models change with evidence.
